title: Can an XRPL issuer claw back XRP or tokens?
abstract: Primary-source guide to can an xrpl issuer claw back xrp or tokens?. Includes integration considerations and evidence boundaries.
body:
XRPL issuers can claw back eligible issued tokens when the required controls are enabled, but native XRP cannot be clawed back. The documentation distinguishes trust-line token controls from MPT issuance flags. Clawback is an issuer capability, not a general right for any dissatisfied buyer to reverse a payment. [1]

For trust-line tokens, Allow Clawback must be configured under the documented account restrictions before issuance. The documentation also describes incompatibility with the No Freeze setting. MPTs use an issuance-level capability. These different control surfaces are a reason to inspect the actual asset and issuer rather than treating all fungible tokens as interchangeable. [1]

For an agent wallet, I recommend surfacing issuer control risk when selecting a payment asset. Separate a seller refund from an issuer clawback and from expiration-based escrow cancellation. A service should not promise automatic recovery merely because the token standard includes a clawback feature. Whether an issuer can or will act in a particular dispute needs separate legal and operational evidence. [1]

Exercise the configured capability on a testing token, a token without it and a native XRP transaction. Record the issuer and issuance configuration used. Do not generalize from those tests to a named stablecoin without examining its real settings. These recommendations derive from the documented controls and intentionally avoid asserting that any issuer has a universal legal entitlement to recover funds in every jurisdiction. [1]
